item.title: Three-dimensional DXA for compartment-specific assessment of proximal femoral bone in type 2 diabetes and diabetic kidney disease
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: 3D-DXA from routine hip DXA captured compartment-specific bone differences across diabetes-kidney status groups in T2DM and DKD, supporting its further evaluation as a compartment-specific imaging adjunct to aBMD in DKD where aBMD is limited. Prospective fracture-outcome studies are required for clinical translation.

item.title: When Copper Falls: Overriding the Irving-Williams Stability Trend Through Outer-Sphere Hydrogen Bonding
item.description: The Irving-Williams series (Mn < Fe < Co < Ni < Cu > Zn) is a well-established thermodynamic stability trend among high-spin divalent first-row transition-metal complexes. However, complete isostructural Mn-Zn series are rare, and those that enable direct evaluation of a defined secondary coordination sphere are even rarer. As a result, whether outer-sphere noncovalent interactions can alter this periodic trend without changing the primary coordination environment has remained unresolved. Here,...

item.title: Clopidogrel Versus Aspirin Monotherapy According to Atherothrombotic Risk Profile
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: After completion of dual antiplatelet therapy following PCI, clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with lower ischemic risk than aspirin in patients with higher atherothrombotic risk, without increased bleeding.

item.description: Atomically thin amorphous carbon holds considerable promise for application in data storage, microelectronics, protective coatings, and flexible electronics. However, its device integration has been hindered by existing direct growth routes that rely on metal catalysts in contact with the substrate, causing metallic residue, film non-uniformity, and the need for post-growth processing. Here, we report the direct growth of monolayer amorphous carbon on a 2-inch sapphire wafer via thermal chemical...

item.title: Adenine Promotes Osteogenic Differentiation and Suppresses Osteoclastogenesis
item.description: Estrogen deficiency disrupts the balance between osteoblast-mediated bone formation and osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, resulting in progressive bone loss. Although AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) regulates the differentiation and activity of both skeletal cell lineages, the role of endogenous purine metabolites in this process remains poorly understood. We investigated adenine responses and AMPK-associated signaling in skeletal-cell models and assessed histological and protein changes...

item.title: 6-Hydroxyrubiadin Regulates TNF-α-Induced MUC5AC Gene Expression via Affecting NF-κB and MAPK Signaling Pathways in Human Airway Epithelial Cells
item.description: In this study, we aimed to investigate whether 6-hydroxyrubiadin (6-HR), a compound derived from the root of Rubia akane Nakai, exerts a regulatory effect on the gene expression of MUC5AC mucin under conditions mimicking pulmonary inflammation in human airway epithelial cells. Confluent NCI-H292 cells were pretreated with 6-HR for 30 min, followed by stimulation with tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α for 24 h. MUC5AC mRNA expression and glycoprotein production were measured using reverse...

item.title: Super Photostable Organic Dye for Single Molecule Imaging and Single Particle Tracking in Live Cells
item.description: Photobleaching of organic fluorophores limits live-cell single-molecule imaging by truncating trajectories and biasing quantitative analyses of membrane protein dynamics. We recently found that photobluing of Alexa Fluor 647 yields a super-photostable red-emitting species, which we named Phoenix Fluor 555 (PF555). This chapter describes two practical workflows for prolonged single-molecule imaging and single-particle tracking of plasma-membrane proteins using a TIRF microscope. In Protocol A,...

item.title: The Associations of Plasma Brain-derived Neurotrophic Factor with Macular Structure and Visual Function in Open-angle Glaucoma: A Cross-sectional Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Plasma BDNF level differed across OAG disease stages and was associated with visual and structural parameters. Among younger patients, plasma BDNF quartile was associated with the fitted csGCCT-BCVA relationship. These cross-sectional findings do not establish temporal or causal relationships.

item.title: Apolipoproteins in nanoparticle-mediated brain drug delivery: promise, mechanisms, and misconceptions
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Apolipoprotein E (apoE) plays a context-dependent role in nanomedicine for central nervous system drug delivery. It can facilitate cerebral endothelial recognition and increase brain exposure in nanoparticle systems while simultaneously promoting hepatic uptake, challenging its traditional interpretation as a brain-specific targeting ligand.

item.title: Serial ultrasound assessment of flexor carpi ulnaris and biceps brachii cross-sectional area in critically ill patients: A prospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Serial ultrasound documented decreases in FCU and BB CSA in this small cohort, with an exploratory direct comparison identifying a greater proportional FCU decrease on day 7. These findings support further evaluation of FCU ultrasound as an additional muscle-monitoring measure. Its value for earlier detection of muscle wasting or diagnosis of ICU-acquired weakness requires direct validation.

item.title: Synergistic effects of docetaxel and anti-PD-L1 therapy on prostate cancer cells: Modulation of apoptosis and PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway
item.description: CONCLUSION: Docetaxel and anti-PD-L1 combination therapy synergistically enhances apoptosis and disrupts key resistance mechanisms in PCa, offering a promising avenue for advanced prostate cancer treatment.

item.title: Two-color, laser-induced fluorometry for evaluating the efficiency of click chemistry-based labeling of extracellular vesicles
item.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs), including exosomes, have attracted considerable attention as promising biomarkers for the early diagnosis and prognosis of cancer. In this study we evaluated the efficiency of a click chemistry-based EV labeling method using a two-color laser-induced fluorometry (LIF) system. During cell culture, cellular membranes were metabolically functionalized with azide groups, and the released EVs were subsequently labeled with Cy5 via click chemistry. The collected EVs were...

item.title: Tailored Methods to Develop High-Performance Chemigenetic Indicators
item.description: Fluorescent indicators are a powerful toolkit in biology to visualize spatiotemporal dynamics of analytes in live cells or tissues. Although indicators based on green fluorescent protein (GFP) and their analogs are well established, they have some limitations, such as low brightness in the red region of the spectrum. To address this issue, so-called chemigenetic indicators that are composed of a synthetic fluorescent ligand and a genetically encoded protein are attracting attention, which can in...

item.title: Genetically Encoded Multimeric Nanoparticles for Measuring Intracellular Diffusion and Cytoplasmic Viscosity
item.description: The crowded cytoplasmic environment affects the transport and reactions of macromolecular complexes at the mesoscale (10-100 nm). Cytoplasmic viscosity correlates with, or even controls, cellular physiology and cellular states. Quantitative measurement of intracellular diffusion is therefore important. Such measurements require inert probes of defined size that do not perturb the cellular environment. Genetically Encoded Multimeric Nanoparticles (GEMs) meet these requirements. GEMs are...

item.title: The calm before the storm: Silence compresses subsequent visual time without reducing temporal precision
item.description: Silence is often conceptualized as the mere absence of auditory input; however, accumulating evidence suggests that the omission and offset of sound are processed as psychologically salient perceptual events. This study investigated whether an abrupt transition from sound to silence biases the perceived duration of subsequently presented visual stimuli. Across four psychophysical experiments, participants performed forced-choice temporal discrimination tasks in which a brief silent interval...

item.title: A Modeling and Simulation Approach to Predicting Oral Absorption of a Weakly Basic Drug: Impact of Acid-Reducing Agents and Storage-Induced Increases in Free Drug Form
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Overall, this simulation model provides a practical approach for predicting gastric pH-dependent oral absorption while accounting for storage-induced changes in free drug form, and will contribute to more efficient formulation design and clinical development.

item.title: Treatment Options After Recurrence Following Perioperative Durvalumab Plus FLOT for Gastric and Gastroesophageal Junction Adenocarcinoma: A Biology-First Sequencing Framework
item.description: Perioperative durvalumab plus fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, and docetaxel (FLOT) has established a new curative-intent standard for resectable gastric and gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma. Recurrence after this regimen creates a clinically distinct, pre-exposed metastatic state for which no prospective sequencing standard exists. Because direct post-D-FLOT evidence is absent, treatment decisions should distinguish exposure-analogous evidence from extrapolation from conventional...

item.title: Navigating result disclosure in the context of reproductive genetic carrier screening: an interview study of genetic healthcare professionals in Belgium
item.description: CONCLUSION: Our findings highlight broad support for current reporting practices in Belgium, while identifying remaining challenges such as the need to expand counselling capacity to ensure responsible and sustainable implementation of RGCS in Belgium.

item.title: Short-pitch dividing method for robotic liver resection: a conceptual shift to close-to-open separation from open-to-close crushing
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates a novel robotic parenchymal transection technique centered on the short-pitch dividing method, representing a conceptual shift from traditional "open-to-close" crushing techniques. This approach minimizes structural injury, and improves procedural efficiency, supporting its utility in RLR.

item.title: Real-world outcomes of glofitamab monotherapy in heavily pretreated patients with relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: A multicenter Korean cohort
item.description: Glofitamab, a CD20×CD3 bispecific antibody, has shown durable activity in relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (RR-DLBCL), but real-world data from Korean patients and after CAR-T failure remain limited. We retrospectively analyzed 46 patients with RR-DLBCL treated with glofitamab monotherapy. Response and safety were assessed in all patients, whereas the main survival and prognostic analyses were conducted in the non-bridge-intent cohort (n = 41), excluding five bridge-intent...

item.title: Pedicle-dural sac congruence and its relationship to pedicle dysplasia in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: A quantitative analysis using an image recognition-assisted gaussian process curve model
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: We quantitatively validated the dysplastic concave pedicle in AIS does not merely lie adjacent to the dural sac, but conforms to its geometric contour. This congruence strongly correlates with the severity of pedicle narrowing. Therefore, our results support the hypothesis that dysplastic pedicle narrowing in AIS represents a morphological adaptation, occurring in association with spatial competition with the deviated dural sac within the rotated vertebral canal.

item.title: Gut Microbiome Signatures and Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Response in Gastrointestinal Cancers: Reproducibility and Translational Readiness
item.description: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Gut microbial features have been associated with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) outcomes, but whether these signatures are robust across gastrointestinal (GI) tumor types, treatment regimens, and populations remains uncertain. This critical narrative review assesses human evidence, experimental mechanisms, longitudinal sampling, and the criteria needed for clinical implementation.

item.description: Advanced anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC) is a rare human papillomavirus-associated malignancy with historically limited prospective evidence for systemic therapy. item.description: Medical documentation, including reply letters from specialty to primary care, imposes a substantial burden on clinicians. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) may help alleviate this burden. This study aims to develop an instruction-tuned LLM to generate reply letters by integrating five types of electronic medical record documents: admission notes, progress notes, procedure notes, operative notes, and discharge summaries. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective Japanese cohort, ILD was observed more frequently in patients receiving enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab than in those receiving enfortumab vedotin monotherapy. Careful monitoring and early recognition of ILD are warranted during combination therapy.

item.title: Longitudinal plasma osimertinib concentrations during treatment in patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC: a prospective real-world study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Higher early osimertinib exposure was observed in patients who subsequently required dose reduction because of toxicity. Plasma concentration measurement may provide complementary information on individual drug exposure when assessing tolerability. Long-term treatment was observed across a broad concentration range following dose modification.

item.description: The OASIS trial [Japan Cancer Treatment Optimization group (JACTOP)-01] is a multicenter, randomized, open-label, phase III study optimizing adjuvant osimertinib therapy for patients with completely resected, epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated (exon 19 deletion or L858R) stage II-III non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer. item.title: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Bone Cancers, 1990 to 2023, With Forecasts to 2050: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this systematic analysis, the burden of bone cancer varied by age, geography, and time, underscoring global disparities. These findings provide valuable insights to inform health system planning and resource allocation tailored to different settings.

item.title: Ultrasonography (IOTA-ADNEX) vs magnetic resonance imaging (ADNEX MR) for diagnosing ovarian cancer in high-risk patients: a prospective study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The IOTA-ADNEX model and ADNEX MR scoring system demonstrated comparable diagnostic accuracy for differentiating benign from malignant adnexal masses in this study. Results appeared to be consistent when stratified by lesion morphology. Both modalities may be used for second-line assessment of masses deemed at risk of malignancy in the first-line ultrasound examination, depending on resources in specific centers. © 2026 The Author(s). item.title: Development and evaluation of a 221Fr atomic source using 225Ac covered with an Y layer for permanent electric dipole moment searches
item.description: We demonstrated the production of high-intensity and low-energy neutral francium (Fr221) by developing an atomic source based on actinium (Ac225) covered with an yttrium (Y) layer. Low-energy Fr+221 ions and neutral Fr221 atoms were produced and measured. We investigated the flux and number of Fr221 atoms from the experimental results under different experimental conditions. The proposed atomic source is promising for Fr trapping experiments and Fr electric dipole moment measurements.

item.description: Hydrogen-bonded glycerol-ethanol (Gly-EtOH) mixtures are promising biodiesel-derived solvents for orange essential oil (OEO) separation. However, how solvent composition governs equilibrium and transport properties and selectivity remains unclear. We combined rotational rheometry, ReaxFF molecular dynamics (ReaxFF-MD), density functional theory (DFT), COSMO-RS, Redlich-Kwong equation of state (RK EoS), and machine learning to establish structure-property-separation relationships. item.title: High-Entropy Lanthanoid Oxide Catalysts for Oxidative Coupling of Methane
item.description: High-entropy engineering of metal oxides provides a powerful platform for developing highly active and structurally robust catalysts; however, its application to heterogenous catalysis that requires stringent selectivity control remains largely unexplored. The low-temperature oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) demands catalysts that combine structural stability with precise tuning of surface basic strength. Here, we report a high-entropy lanthanoid oxide catalyst, (LaSmEuGdDy)0.4O3, synthesized...

item.title: Unveiling the Active Aluminum Sites and Confinement Effects of Zeolites for N2O Decomposition
item.description: The development of sustainable catalysts for nitrous oxide (N2O) decomposition remains a significant challenge in environmental chemistry and is traditionally reliant on transition-metal-based active sites. Herein, we establish that aluminosilicate zeolites themselves are highly effective catalysts for this reaction. item.title: Total Synthesis, Absolute Configurational Determination, and Antifouling Activity Evaluation of Cretenyne B
item.description: The relative configuration of the tetrahydrofuran moiety in cretenyne B (2) has been previously determined. However, the stereochemistries at the C6 and C13 side-chain positions of 2 remain unresolved. Herein, we report the absolute configuration of 2 using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) analysis and total synthesis, and the antifouling activity of two candidate diastereomers for 2. item.description: Muscle power is essential for functional capacity in older adults and can be improved through power-focused resistance training (PRT). PRT adaptations are load- and velocity-specific, yet optimal load prescription remains unclear. As force and velocity capacities vary between individuals, this 12-week intervention compared two force-velocity (F-V) profile-guided loading strategies: training at loads matched versus not matched to the F-V deficit. F-V profiles of 80 adults ≥ 65 years were assessed...

item.title: Ultra-Efficient Memristive Voltage-Resistance Logic Framework With Integrated Readout Strategy Based on Hafnium Zirconium Oxide
item.description: The integration of logic operations and data storage is regarded as a promising strategy for enabling edge computing, a key requirement for real-time, data-intensive scientific and industrial applications. Achieving edge-capable computing, however, requires exceptional spatiotemporal efficiency, and many previously proposed logic schemes still face substantial limitations. item.title: Radical initiators triggered by red light irradiation
item.description: A radical initiation method using red light irradiation was developed. Zinc(II) tetraphenylporphyrin and a thiohydroxamate ester generate a carbon-centered radical that starts a chain reaction. The method was validated by conducting Ueno-Stork cyclizations. The room-temperature reaction conditions are mild and the reaction can be scaled up to the gram scale in a batch system.

item.title: EWSR1 associates with the 40S ribosomal subunit and represses translation to maintain endoplasmic reticulum homeostasis
item.description: FET family proteins (FUS, EWSR1, and TAF15) have garnered significant attention due to their involvement in oncogenic fusions and mutations in various cancers and neurodegenerative disorders. Although these highly conserved RNA-binding proteins are widely described as multifunctional regulators of gene expression, their precise molecular functions remain incompletely understood. Here, we uncover a previously unrecognized role for EWSR1 as a selective translational repressor in cancer cells....

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Adding routinely available intraoperative and early postoperative variables produced modest but consistent improvements in postoperative risk prediction compared with preoperative variables alone. However, facility-specific variation in calibration limits direct transportability of absolute risk estimates. The models may support prioritization for postoperative clinical reassessment, but exploratory decision curve analysis did not establish a specific intervention or triage...

item.title: A Behavior Change Technique-Based Text Messaging Intervention for Obesity Among Employed Adult Men Younger Than 40 Years: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The findings support the feasibility and acceptability of an SMS text messaging intervention for health guidance among employed men younger than 40 years with obesity, although evidence of its effectiveness remains preliminary. Further research with larger samples is needed to evaluate its effectiveness and optimize the intervention.

item.title: Preservation of Vascular Tissues From Shrinkage During X-Ray 3D-CECT Imaging
item.description: Preventing shrinkage of biological tissues during X-ray microfocus computed tomography (3D-microCT) is essential to prevent motion artifacts and microstructural changes, which is particularly problematic in the context of 4D-microCT. While liquid immersion and parafilm wrapping are commonly used to limit dehydration, both methods present limitations for combining them with in situ mechanical testing. This work introduces an in-house environmental stage capable of controlling temperature and...

item.title: Acute exercise for emotional pattern separation in youth with psychiatric symptoms and childhood adversity: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: Adolescence and young adulthood are critical periods for the emergence of transdiagnostic psychiatric symptoms. Pattern separation (PS) is the ability to discriminate between similar stimuli. Its behavioral proxy is mnemonic discrimination. PS is an important hippocampal function impaired in several mental disorders. Previous research demonstrated that while childhood adversity might lead to impaired PS, acute exercise could enhance it. item.title: Label-Free Raman Imaging Defines Distinct Cell Populations in Human Skin
item.description: Understanding cellular heterogeneity in human skin is crucial for regenerative medicine and tissue engineering. In this study, we applied label-free Raman imaging to visualize molecular features corresponding to the three-dimensional architecture of the epidermis. Spatially resolved Raman spectra, combined with multivariate data analysis, enabled the identification of cell-layer-specific molecular signatures. item.description: Dictyostelium discoideum is a key Amoebozoa model organism in cell biology, offering unique insights into chemotaxis, cell polarity and the transition from unicellular to multicellular life. item.title: A research framework for evaluating upstream multimodal sarcopenia risk domains in older adults
item.description: Established sarcopenia definitions identify clinically important impairment, but their thresholds are not designed to characterize all biological changes associated with subsequent muscle decline. Whether additional measurements improve assessment before these thresholds are reached remains uncertain. This structured narrative review proposes a research framework for evaluating upstream, multimodal sarcopenia risk domains in older adults. It integrates diagnostic consensus statements with...

item.description: Meniscal preservation is essential for the maintenance of knee function. A catalytic amount of copper-(I) salt efficiently promotes the 1,3-shift of a propargyl group from an oxygen atom to a carbon atom in an aryl magnesium species, affording phenol derivatives having a propargyl group at the ortho position, which are otherwise difficult to synthesize. item.description: Excessive free radical production and dysregulated immune responses contribute to myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury. item.description: T4 RNA Ligase 1 (Rnl1) catalyzes the ligation of a 5'-phosphate to a 3'-hydroxyl in single-stranded RNA and is widely used in RNA biotechnology for applications such as RNA library preparation and 3'-adapter ligation. item.description: CONCLUSION: For Australian women who give birth in the private system, risk factors for poorer breastfeeding outcomes include older age and primiparity. Women who present with these characteristics may benefit from targeted breastfeeding support.

item.description: Cognitive reappraisal refers to changing how one thinks about a situation to alter its emotional impact. item.description: Efficient DNA replication requires coordinated use of replicative and error-prone polymerases, which provide flexibility at the cost of mutagenesis. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Advancing equitable neurogenic rehabilitation requires integrating intercultural pragmatics and sociocultural perspectives into assessment and treatment. Approaches such as dynamic assessment, holistic assessment, and telehealth offer practical pathways to improve assessment practices for individuals with acquired social communication disorders.

item.description: The ability to discriminate experiences in memory is an important indicator of cognitive health in older age and a sensitive marker of hippocampal integrity. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that under the specific locally deployed multiagent configuration tested, LLMs can generate a range of context-sensitive therapeutic responses but showed limitations in producing high-quality meaning-making interventions. item.title: Feasibility and equity in the assessment of parent-child interactions: Lessons from three approaches
item.description: Observations of parent-child interactions provide critical insights that directly inform developmental theory and treatment initiatives. Equitable and feasible assessment is necessary to fully understand the spectrum of relevant parent and child behaviors accounting for cultural, ethnic, racial, and linguistic diversity. Parent-child observational research has primarily relied on structured, in-person recordings later coded by research assistants. This approach introduces logistical barriers for...

item.title: The diversity within: Exploring disability identity, self-efficacy, and belonging among university students with disabilities
item.description: CONCLUSION/IMPLICATIONS: The findings support a psychosocial and relational model of disability identity and the importance of recognizing heterogeneity in disability identity development among university students. The results have implications for researchers, educators, and institutions seeking to foster more inclusive, relationally responsive learning environments in higher education. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

item.title: Nanoplastics as Hepatic Toxicant Vectors: Interactions with Environmental Chemicals, Organelle Dysfunction, and Regulated Cell Death
item.description: The environmental accumulation of nanoplastics (NPs) raises concerns regarding their potential effects on hepatic function. Experimental studies suggest that NP exposure can be related with altered mitochondrial electron transport chain activity, reduced ATP availability, changes in Keap1/Nrf2-mediated antioxidant responses, and impaired mitophagy. NPs have also been linked to cytoskeletal alterations, disrupted autophagic flux, and metabolic disturbances that can contribute to processes...

item.title: Trends in Supportive Medication Use Before, During, and After Dexmedetomidine Initiation in End-of-Life Palliative Care: A Descriptive Follow-up Study
item.description: Dexmedetomidine's benefits include opioid sparing, low respiratory impact and potential to maintain lucidity in those nearing end-of-life (EoL). This study aims to characterize the impact of dexmedetomidine infusion on EoL supportive psychotropic and pain medications. Investigators conducted a retrospective chart review of patients approaching EoL receiving dexmedetomidine infusion between January 2020 and December 2023. The primary outcome was concomitant medication dosing over the course of...

item.title: Phase 1 study of OX40 agonist ABBV-368 as monotherapy or in combination with budigalimab in advanced solid tumors
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: ABBV-368 with/without budigalimab was well tolerated and induced dose-specific immune cell activation in advanced solid tumors. Further combination or optimization strategies are required for meaningful clinical benefit.

item.title: Development of a Corneal Biomechanical Risk Score for Visual Field Progression in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This internally validated, exploratory risk score based on four corneal biomechanical parameters stratified POAG patients by risk of VF progression. Further validation is needed to determine its clinical utility.

item.title: Depicting External Crown Resorption in Syndromic Amelogenesis Imperfecta Associated With Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
item.description: CONCLUSION: ECR can affect primary and permanent dentition, leading to tooth loss if left unrestored. The radiographic screening protocol for early diagnosis and treatment of ECR proposed in this article can aid in preserving teeth.

item.title: The delocalized nature of chemical bonding at a catalytic metal surface
item.description: Adsorbate bonding at metal surfaces requires hybridization of localized molecular orbitals with delocalized electronic bands of the metal; hence, the electronic wave function involved in bonding may extend far beyond the adsorption site. We revealed the consequence of this delocalization by determining the distance over which structural variations of the metal surface influence the molecule-metal bond strength. Velocity-resolved kinetics provided adsorption energies for three molecules bound at...

item.title: Spatial coordination in the codevelopment of the human urogenital system during organogenesis
item.description: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium-derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of...

item.title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
item.description: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development-its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and...

item.title: Constructing the history of a contested regionTHE CAULDRON: Simon Sebag Montefiore Weidenfeld & Nicolson, 2026. 528 pp
item.description: A lack of source notes undermines an otherwise illuminating overview of the Middle East.

item.title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
item.description: Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This...

item.title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
item.description: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles. We found that species in highly developed and water-managed...

item.title: Whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate, Danionella cerebrum
item.description: A complete cell type transcriptome atlas of a vertebrate could promote understanding of animal cell type composition, organization, and evolution. The miniaturized, transparent, and regenerative teleost Danionella cerebrum brings whole-vertebrate single-cell profiling experiments within reach. We performed region-stratified single-cell RNA sequencing across the adult Danionella body and mapped cell types and gene expression at single-cell resolution using spatial transcriptomics. We delineated...

item.title: Vaccine immunity can drive eosinophil recruitment in influenza breakthrough infection with mouse strain-specific outcomes
item.description: Eosinophils are pleiotropic cells and can respond to a wide array of inflammatory stimuli, including respiratory viral infection. Although they are historically associated with adverse outcomes in vaccinated hosts after breakthrough infection, such as during vaccine-associated enhanced respiratory disease (VAERD) for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), eosinophils can also help mediate antiviral immunity. We previously observed mild, nonpathological lung eosinophilia in vaccinated mice...

item.title: A comparative analysis of baseline and post-intervention surveillance in a hookworm control pilot: Evidence from Tiantai County, Zhejiang Province, 2022-2024
item.description: Hookworm infection remains a neglected tropical disease in rural areas where low-level transmission may persist despite long-term control efforts. This repeated cross-sectional study evaluated changes in hookworm infection in six rural villages of Tiantai County, Zhejiang Province, China, before and after implementation of an integrated control program. In 2022, approximately 200 permanent residents aged ≥3 years were sampled from each village for the baseline survey. After one year of...

item.title: Somapacitan Treatment in Children and Adolescents Born SGA: Two-Year Efficacy and Preference Over Daily GH
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In children born SGA, once-weekly somapacitan maintained efficacy through 2 years, with safety comparable to daily GH, and was preferred after switching.

item.title: Synthetic auxotrophy reveals metabolic regulation of plasma cell generation, affinity maturation, and cytokine receptor signaling
item.description: The proliferation and development of activated B lymphocytes into antibody (Ab)-secreting plasma cells are critical determinants of humoral immunity and sustain certain autoimmune diseases. Specific pathways and substrate supplies in intermediary metabolism influence lymphocyte differentiation and function. We now show that although stringent restriction of glutamine supply decreases B cell proliferation and differentiation into plasma cells, glutaminolysis - a major metabolic use of this amino...

item.title: A chemomechanical bifurcation landscape unifies sustained growth, length homeostasis, and regenerative collapse in axons
item.description: Axonal growth machinery is largely shared across neurons, but axons exhibit strikingly different fates depending on developmental and environmental context: sustained elongation in peripheral neurons under permissive conditions, length homeostasis in cortical neurons after target innervation, and pathological collapse into dystrophic endbulbs in injured adult central nervous system (CNS) axons. These divergent outcomes have resisted explanation by length-sensing and biomechanical models that...

item.title: Global bee bioregions mirror those of other taxa despite a uniquely bimodal latitudinal diversity gradient
item.description: Bioregionalization, the partitioning of the globe into areas of biotic similarity, is one of nature's most striking patterns, and highly congruent boundaries have been identified across plants, tetrapods, ants, and butterflies. However, these taxa also share a unimodal latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG), raising the question of whether bioregionalization and the LDG are mechanistically coupled or instead arise from largely independent processes acting on different timescales. Bees...

item.title: Complexity functions of infinite sequences
item.description: We address the inverse problem for complexity functions of infinite words, which asks which functions can occur as complexity functions of infinite words. We survey our recent advances on this problem and several of its ramifications. We describe an asymptotic solution to the inverse problem, realizing every function satisfying two necessary conditions as the complexity function of an infinite word up to asymptotic equivalence. We then turn to phenomena beyond asymptotic equivalence, presenting...

item.title: Direct atomic-scale observation reveals rare earth element fractionation at mineral-water interfaces
item.description: Clay minerals, ubiquitous across diverse geological systems, exert fundamental controls on critical geochemical processes, particularly through their adsorptive interactions with economically vital elements such as heavy rare earth elements (HREEs). The adsorption of HREEs onto clay surfaces is not only the key process that enriches these critical resources but also a potential archive for dating significant weathering events. However, the atomic-scale mechanisms governing the preferential...

item.title: Ddx3x deficiency in mice impairs corticofugal motor circuits and causes motor deficits that are attenuated by early-life exercise
item.description: The X-linked RNA helicase DDX3X is a high-risk gene for autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability primarily in females. Individuals with pathogenic variants in DDX3X have pervasive and often severe motor manifestations. Using mouse models, we studied the circuits underlying the motor phenotypes associated with Ddx3x deficiency and examined the feasibility of an early intervention to ameliorate motor trajectories. We show that Ddx3x controls both the development and later plasticity of...

item.title: Crowding limits relative bacterial surface accumulation with density-induced effective heating
item.description: The accumulation of microswimmers near walls has been studied for decades. While hydrodynamics and single-cell kinematics are well-explored, the role of cell-cell interactions remains understudied. However, in realistic, crowded environments such as the human gut, these interactions can be just as crucial. Here, we demonstrate that they actively weaken bacterial surface accumulation. Analysis of entrapped cell tracks reveals that crowding enhances orientational fluctuations, which increase the...

item.title: Acute Chagas disease from probable oral ingestion of Trypanosoma cruzi in the United States - high risk for severe disease
item.description: No abstract

item.title: A candidate genetic trigger of female sex determination in Marsabit clawed frogs (Xenopus borealis)
item.description: A central question in biology asks why the genetic basis of sex determination evolves quickly in some groups even though disruption of this process carries severe risks such as sterility. A challenge to understanding mechanisms of this rapid evolution is a lack of functionally verified genetic triggers of sex determination. To begin to remedy this, we set out to identify, characterize, and functionally test the genetic trigger of female sex determination in Marsabit clawed frogs (Xenopus...

item.title: Autochthonous Acute Chagas Disease with Fulminant Myocarditis in a Texas Infant Exposed to a Peridomestic Environment with Trypanosoma cruzi-infected Vectors and Animals
item.description: We describe a case of autochthonous acute Chagas disease in an infant with fulminant myocarditis requiring aggressive support. Peridomestic investigation revealed Trypanosoma cruzi-infected vectors and animals. This highlights the importance of (1) early diagnosis and treatment and (2) understanding the epidemiological risk factors for Chagas disease in the United States.

item.title: A target-domain augmentation and class-wise alignment framework for few-shot cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis
item.description: Cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis often has to adapt to a new operating condition with only a few labelled target samples. This setting creates two coupled problems. First, the sparse target support set cannot describe the target fault distribution sufficiently. Second, the same fault class may occupy different feature regions across source and target conditions, which weakens source-domain pretrained classifiers. Existing methods usually improve few-shot learning or reduce domain shift,...

item.title: Ataxin-2 loss flips a metabolic switch for neuron health
item.description: Gastaldo et al.¹ report that lowering ataxin-2 protects neurons from TDP-43 toxicity in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis by activating neuronal glycolysis and astrocytic cholesterol synthesis, not by reversing TDP-43-dependent molecular pathology. The downstream effectors, IDH1 and HMGCS1, thus emerge as candidate therapeutic targets.

item.title: Molecular insights into the activation mechanism of the slow anion channel AtSLAH3
item.description: The plant slow anion channel SLAH3 regulates essential physiological processes, including stomatal closure and stress responses, yet the structural mechanism underlying its activation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the activation mechanism of SLAH3 by determining cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of the wild-type (WT) channel and gain-of-function mutants identified through a targeted mutagenesis screen of pore-lining residues. Notably, the L400A mutant was captured...

item.title: A stress-adapted fiber state promotes clonal expansion of deleted mitochondrial DNA
item.description: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) depletion and multiple deletions frequently coexist in mitochondrial disease, neurodegeneration, and aging, yet how the two relate and why deletions accumulate focally remain unresolved. Here, longitudinal bulk and in situ analyses of Mpv17^(-/-) murine muscle reveal that a compensatory rise in mitochondrial transcripts per mtDNA initially offsets severe, uniform mtDNA depletion, preserving the respiratory chain. However, this response carries a delayed cost: by six...

item.title: IFN-γ and proinflammatory cytokines induce astrocyte programs that support antigen-dependent CD4<sup>+</sup> T cell restimulation
item.description: Astrocyte contributions to CNS antigen presentation remain poorly defined. We show that interferon gamma (IFN-γ, the sole type II interferon), with proinflammatory cytokines, induces astrocytes to express components mediating attraction of and antigen presentation to CD4^(+) T cells. Re-analysis of astrocyte-enriched single-cell sequencing from bacterial mimetic-injected mice revealed a transcriptionally distinct, IFN-responsive astrocyte population enriched for antigen-presentation genes 24 h...

item.title: Sense-and-respond: Engineered bacteria drive epithelial repair during gut inflammation
item.description: Zhao et al.¹ engineer a reactive oxygen species-responsive probiotic strain of Escherichia coli that senses intestinal inflammation and responds by locally delivering IL-22-Fc to promote epithelial repair, establishing an integrated sense-and-respond platform for inflammatory bowel disease diagnosis and mucosal healing.

item.title: Acute respiratory distress syndrome FXR/Sptlc2 signaling promotes alveolar macrophage mitophagy and limits lung inflammation
item.description: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) undergo functional reprogramming that critically regulates lung inflammation. Although mitophagy is essential for mitochondrial quality control, its role in macrophage functional reprogramming during acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains unclear. Here, we identify the nuclear receptor Nr1h4 (FXR) as a transcriptional regulator of mitophagy in AMs. FXR activation transcriptionally upregulates serine palmitoyltransferase long chain base subunit 2 (Sptlc2),...

item.title: Locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons have diverse activity patterns across species and biological context
item.description: The locus coeruleus (LC) brainstem cell group is evolutionarily conserved across vertebrates and influences both mind (cognition) and body (cardiorespiratory, metabolic, and immune functions) via two-putatively distinct-spontaneous activity patterns. Yet, the degree to which spontaneous LC firing rates and patterns are homogeneous across species has never been assessed due to inherently limited sample sizes. To remedy this, we pooled cross-species data from 20 laboratories to show that firing...

item.title: ALS-linked FUS mutation impairs GEMIN5-dependent mRNA recruitment to neuronal late endosomes
item.description: Neurons depend on tightly regulated positioning of cellular components to maintain long-distance signaling, but the mechanisms guiding specific mRNAs to distant regions remain unclear. Here, we show that late endosomes function as selective RNA carriers in human motor neurons and uncover the molecular logic guiding their loading. Using APEX2-mediated proximity labeling, we identify the external transcriptome of RAB7A-positive endosomes and find a specific population of mRNAs enriched for...

item.title: Mesenchymal stem cells inhibit ferroptosis in dopaminergic neurons of Parkinson's disease mice by phosphorylating STAT6
item.description: Ferroptosis is recognized as a critical driver of dopaminergic neuronal injury. Emerging evidence suggests that the neuroprotective effects of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells are partially mediated through signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6) signaling. However, few studies have investigated whether bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells can modulate ferroptosis in dopaminergic neurons, and the specific regulatory role of STAT6 in neuronal ferroptosis remains poorly...

item.title: Arousal-related neural circuits in consciousness disorders: Updated model integrating ascending reticular activating system and mesocircuit
item.description: Consciousness emerges from the dynamic coupling of arousal and conscious content. Although the ascending reticular activating system predominantly regulates arousal, mesocircuit activity supports the integration of conscious content. Disorders of consciousness arise primarily from structural damage or functional disruption of these two core neural systems. Recent advances in neuroscience have enabled high-resolution mechanistic investigations of disorders of consciousness at the cellular and...

item.title: Rethinking Laboratory Screening for Patients Receiving Biologics
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Does time-lapse imaging (TLI) of embryos improve reproductive outcomes in in vitro fertilisation (IVF)/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI)? Individual participant data (IPD) meta-analysis
item.description: BACKGROUND: Time‑lapse imaging (TLI) systems may improve the success of in vitro fertilisation (IVF)/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) by enabling undisturbed embryo culture and/or providing morphokinetic data to refine embryo selection. Despite several trials and aggregate meta-analyses showing uncertainty of benefit, there is little translation of evidence into guidelines. Heterogeneity in participant populations and algorithms used for TLI, although acknowledged in aggregate...

item.title: Community Health Worker Interventions Addressing Social Determinants of Health in Chronic Disease: A Systematic Review
item.description: CONCLUSION: CHW-led interventions show promise for addressing social needs and improving engagement in care among adults with chronic disease, but evidence of meaningful clinical benefit is still limited. The lack of large, well-powered trials underscores the need for more rigorous research to strengthen the evidence base for CHW-driven SDOH interventions in US health systems.

item.title: Protection against violence and boundary violations in medical institutions: An institutional safeguarding concept of an Austrian university clinic for child and adolescent psychiatry
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The sustainable integration of safeguarding concepts in medical institutions requires targeted implementation strategies and the systematic consideration of institutional barriers. Safeguarding concepts should be conceptualized as participatory, continuous processes of organizational development that integrate reflective practice, strengthen quality assurance, and benefit patients, relatives, and staff.

item.title: Comparative Effects of Pharmacological Treatment on Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: No significant differences among the individual SGLT-2I, GLP-1RA, nsMRA, and sGC drugs were found in risks of CV death, all-cause mortality or SAEs in patients with HFmrEF/HFpEF. Further evidence is needed to support these comparative effects and update guidance on medication choice for HFmrEF/HFpEF.

item.title: Twelve-Month Cumulative Incidence, Characteristics, and Correlates of Non-adherence in Youths Treated with Second-Generation Antipsychotics for Mental Disorders: Results from a Prospective Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: One in four youths starting SGAs (increasing in survival analyses accounting for early dropouts to more than one in three youth) discontinued SGAs against medical advice within 12 months, mainly owing to perceived lack of treatment need. As much as 39% of the non-adherence would have remained undetected without SGA plasma level assessments. Interventions should target patient, caregiver, and medication factors to reduce barriers and improve outcomes.

item.title: Validation of an intrinsic capacity index and the effects of aspirin in older males and females: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
item.description: Chronic low-grade inflammation ("inflammaging") drives age-related decline, but whether anti-inflammatory medications preserve functional performance in older age remains unknown. This study evaluated the 5-year effect of aspirin on a modified Intrinsic Capacity (IC) index in older males and females. A post-hoc analysis of a randomised controlled trial comparing daily 100 mg aspirin to placebo in prolonging dementia- and disability-free survival (DFS) in community-dwelling individuals aged ≥ 65...

item.title: Workforce Retention in Florida's Behavioral Health Sector: A Mixed-Methods Survey Investigation of Positive and Negative Contributors Impacting Intention to Leave
item.description: Florida faces a critical behavioral health workforce shortage, with provider supply falling approximately 14,000 positions short of demand. Understanding the factors that predict workforce attrition is essential for developing targeted retention strategies. This study used a mixed-methods survey design to examine workforce retention among licensed behavioral health professionals in Florida. Surveys were administered to providers across seven professions and all regions of Florida (N = 330)....

item.title: Optogenetic Tool for Controlling p53 Signaling Pathway
item.description: Optogenetics enables precise spatiotemporal control of intracellular processes by light and has become a powerful approach for manipulating cell signaling and gene expression. While chemical induction systems and synthetic biology-based tools such as Tet-regulated promoters and CRISPRa/CRISPRi provide versatile means to control gene expression, their temporal resolution and spatial specificity are limited by diffusion and degradation of chemical stimuli. Optogenetic strategies based on...

item.title: Data-driven reweighting of the Charlson and Elixhauser comorbidity indices using German claims data: development for in-hospital mortality only, external validation across clinical and health-economic outcomes
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Adaptive lasso reweighting consistently enhances the predictive validity of the Charlson and Elixhauser indices across both clinical and health-economic endpoints. Our multi-endpoint evaluation shows consistent performance gains across the three examined German validation cohorts, offering a practical basis for risk adjustment in health-economic studies using German claims data. Because development and validation were based exclusively on German data and a single coding system...

item.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Frailty Index (MBS-FI)
item.description: CONCLUSION: The MBS-FI was internally validated and provided incremental discrimination for several non-mortality outcomes. Improvements for mortality were limited, and external validation and assessment of clinical utility are required before routine use.

item.title: Beyond Cognitive Offloading: A Catholic Theological-Ethical Framework for Human Intelligence, Critical Thinking, and AI Integration within Health-Professional Education
item.description: The growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into medical and health-professions education offers opportunities for personalized learning, access to information, and cognitive support, while raising concerns about cognitive offloading and the potential displacement of critical thinking and independent judgment. This article presents a conceptual and normative theological-ethical analysis of the responsible integration of AI into health-professions education. It draws on a focused,...

item.title: Clinical features and associated factors for porto-sinusoidal vascular disease in primary Sjögren's disease: a retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSION: This exploratory study characterizes the clinical features of pSjD patients with PSVD. A constellation of associated features-long disease duration, splenomegaly with hypersplenism, hepatic synthetic impairment (hypoalbuminemia, INR prolongation, elevated AST/ALP), hypokalemia, and hypergammaglobulinemia-may aid in early identification of portal hypertension. These preliminary findings require validation in large prospective cohorts. Key Points • pSjD may represent an autoimmune...

item.title: Edge structure influences infants' and toddlers' engagement with natural scenes
item.description: Low-level features, or basic visual properties like color, luminance, and orientation, guide visual attention across the lifespan. We evaluated how variations in one low-level feature, edge structure, related to visual attention to natural scenes (i.e., photographs of places such as kitchens and landscapes) across the first two postnatal years of life. Specifically, we asked how the proportion of cardinal edges (i.e., horizontal and vertical) as well as the edge quantity within scenes related to...

item.title: Neddylation is required for cerebellar development in mice
item.description: The cerebellum undergoes a prolonged and highly coordinated developmental program that is essential for motor and cognitive function, yet the post-translational mechanisms governing this process are not fully understood. Here, we identify neddylation, a ubiquitin-like post-translational modification that conjugates NEDD8 to substrate proteins, as a critical regulator of cerebellar development. We show that the indispensable neddylation pathway component NAE1 is broadly expressed in the...

item.title: Trehalose alleviates oxidative stress-induced senescence and is associated with cell-cycle remodeling
item.description: Trehalose has been widely used as a food and drug additive for a long time, and its effects on antioxidant stress, autophagy, and anti-aging have been gradually studied. However, the molecular mechanism by which trehalose exerts anti-oxidative stress and anti-aging effects has not been fully clarified. Our anti-aging cell phenotype study based on trehalose validates its intrinsic mechanisms of anti-oxidative stress and anti-inflammation in cells. We analyzed publicly available transcriptomic...

item.title: S1PR2 antagonist S118 prevents rapid degradation of 5-FU through down-regulation of hepatic dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD)
item.description: Our previous studies showed that activation of S1PR2 (Sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 2) upregulates dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) expression in colorectal cancers, conferring 5-FU resistance. Given that hepatic cells express high levels of S1PR2, this study aimed to investigate the inhibitory effect of S118, S1PR2 antagonist, on hepatic DPD and its consequent impact on 5-FU pharmacokinetics. We revealed that S118 exhibited a favorable pharmacokinetic profile through inhibiting DPD...

item.title: Effects of extracellular vesicles after tibial transverse bone transport on angiogenesis and cardiac function in rats with acute myocardial infarction
item.description: This study aimed to investigate the effects of extracellular vesicles derived from Tibial transverse bone transport (TTT) in diabetic rats on cardiac function, and angiogenesis in rats with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Diabetic rat models of TTT and sham operation were first established. Then, a rat AMI model was established. The Sham-EVs and the TTT-EVs were injected via myocardial injection. After the intervention, echocardiography was used to evaluate cardiac function. Masson staining...

item.title: Cross-Cultural Factorial Validation of the Children's Eating Behavior Questionnaire (CEBQ) in Samoan Children: A Methodological Note
item.description: CONCLUSION: The original CEBQ factor structure was not replicated among Samoan children. The alternative three-factor structure requires confirmation, but the findings underscore the need to establish measurement validity before applying eating behavior instruments across cultural settings.

item.title: Adjunctive therapeutic plasma exchange as rescue therapy in septic shock due to streptococcal infection: a multicentric retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSION: In SRSS, adjunctive TPE was associated with rapid hemodynamic stabilization and improved lactate kinetics. Exploratory adjusted survival analyses support prospective evaluation of TPE in SRSS.

item.title: Computational and experimental study of CuO-ZnO nanocomposite using the plant Peganum harmala L. and their antifungal, antibacterial applications
item.description: The rapid emergence of AMR necessitates the development of novel, sustainable therapeutic agents. This study reports the green synthesis of copper-decorated zinc oxide (CuO-ZnO) nanocomposite using an aqueous leaf extract of Peganum harmala L., which served as a reducing and capping agent. A quantitative EDX analysis confirmed a high loading of Cu of 24.25% (7.09%) mass. Characterization showed that the average primary particle size was 29 ± 1.3 nm, and that the structures were crystalline and...

item.title: Families caring for children and adolescents with rare disease: a health economic evaluation of face-to-face and online psychosocial support intervention of the randomized controlled CARE-FAM-NET study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In the primary analysis, CF and WC were associated with lower mean costs and positive baseline-adjusted QALY differences relative to CG, whereas CF + WC was associated with higher mean costs and a positive baseline-adjusted QALY difference. None of the differences in costs or baseline-adjusted QALYs were statistically significant. The sensitivity analysis yielded broadly comparable findings for CF and WC, whereas results differed for CF + WC. Given the study limitations,...

item.title: Measurement properties of the EQ-5D-5L and SF-6D in measuring the health-related quality of life of non-small cell lung cancer patients on active treatments in China
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Both the EQ-5D-5L and SF-6D have robust measurement properties for assessing health status in Chinese NSCLC patients.

item.title: Dried fish soluble as a functional ingredient in high soybean diets supports gut health and the gut-liver axis of rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) strains
item.description: Supplementing dried fish soluble (FS) in a high soybean meal (SBM)-based diet could ameliorate the adverse impacts of high SBM on fish gut health. This study aimed to determine the impact of supplementing dried FS in the high SBM-based diet on rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) across two strains through gut histology and gut-liver axis-related gene expression. A total of 600 fish (22.1 g) were randomly distributed to 30 tanks (20 fish/tank) in a recirculating aquaculture system following a 2 ×...

item.title: Optimization of two-step asymmetric PCR protocol to prepare single-strand DNA for aptamer screening
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These results contributed to enhancing the efficiency, purity, and yield of ssDNA preparation. Furthermore, statistical analysis identified key factors as primer concentration and ratio, amplification cycles, Mg^(2+) concentration, and annealing temperature. It is recommended that these critical parameters be prioritized during ssDNA preparation by A-PCR in SELEX procedures.

item.title: Sociodemographic and clinicopathologic features associated with rapid relapse in triple-negative breast cancer: a Swedish nationwide registry-based study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Rapid relapse defines a particularly vulnerable TNBC population characterized by aggressive tumor biology, early dissemination, inferior survival, and sociodemographic disadvantage, while lrTNBC represents an intermediate phenotype with delayed disease progression. Distinguishing rrTNBC from lrTNBC may improve risk stratification, guide treatment decisions, and support more personalized follow-up strategies.

item.title: Moderate-to-late preterm birth, common respiratory pathogens, and severe lower respiratory tract infections across childhood
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: MLP birth is associated with severe LRTI outcomes that extend beyond infancy into early and middle childhood. Although no significant differences were detected in pathogen positivity rates between children born MLP and their full-term counterparts, MLP birth showed a significant synergistic additive interaction with RSV infection in relation to greater disease severity.

item.title: Primary healthcare use prior to hospital consultations for spinal disorders among Danish children and adolescents: A descriptive nationwide registry-based study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Patterns of primary healthcare use varied according to parental spine-related hospital diagnoses and comorbidity burden. No clear overall income gradient was observed, although patterns varied by provider type. These findings describe heterogeneous pre-hospital primary healthcare use in this population.

item.title: Prefrontal circuitry abnormalities and cognitive impairment in adolescents with early-onset psychosis
item.description: Early-onset psychosis (EOP) is associated with marked cognitive impairment and poorer health-related and psychosocial outcomes compared to adult-onset illness, yet the neural mechanisms underlying these deficits during adolescence remain incompletely understood. Despite evidence implicating dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) dysfunction, the region's functional and structural correlates in youth with EOP are not well characterized. Adolescents with EOP (N=31) and healthy controls (HC; N=20)...

item.title: Eu-MOF-based sandwich-type magnetic molecularly imprinted fluorescent sensor for sensitive and visual detection of chlorogenic acid in cigar tobacco
item.description: A sandwich-type magnetic molecularly imprinted fluorescent sensor (BA-Eu-MOF-CGA-MIPs) based on europium-based metal-organic frameworks (Eu-MOF) was constructed for highly selective detection of chlorogenic acid (CGA) in cigar tobacco and its products. The sensor integrates magnetic separation (via Fe(3)O(4) nanoparticles), imprinted cavities for specific capture, and boronate-affinity-mediated sandwich structure for fluorescence quenching. Under optimal conditions, a detection limit of 0.96...

item.title: Multi-omics analysis reveals metabolic reprogramming and CTH downregulation in diabetic kidney disease
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings provide insight into DKD pathogenesis and highlight CTH as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target.

item.title: Exploratory analysis of nasal and gut microbial community structure in preschool children with recurrent wheeze
item.description: Early-life wheezing has been associated with microbial alterations along the gut-airway axis, yet few studies have examined bacterial communities in both compartments within the same children. This cross-sectional exploratory pilot study (n=25) characterized nasal and stool bacterial communities in children aged 1-4 years with recurrent wheeze and healthy controls using 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding. Across participants, nasal and stool bacteriomes were highly individualized and taxonomically...

item.title: Radial head arthroplasty restores axial construct stiffness in a Monteggia-like injury model: a biomechanical study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Radial head integrity significantly contributes to forearm stiffness in Monteggia-like lesions. Radial head arthroplasty partially restores biomechanical stability after resection and may alter load distribution in a manner that could be relevant for fixation durability. These findings support the need to address the radial column to optimize stability in complex elbow injuries.

item.title: Arthroplasty centers logistically separated from general orthopedic departments were associated with a more successful implementation of a standardized day-case setup : A Danish cohort study of 6718 procedures from a fast-track multi-center collaboration
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Arthroplasty centers with logistics separate from the general orthopedic department, SACs and EACs, were associated with higher rates of successful DOS discharge among eligible patients during implementation of a standardized day-case pathway, despite integrated arthroplasty units, AUOs, having higher day-case surgery use before implementation.

item.title: Columnar-lined esophagus measuring less than 1 cm as a risk factor for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in Japanese men
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to demonstrate a significant association between USSBE and ESCC. USSBE may help identify individuals at increased risk of ESCC. Exploratory subgroup findings according to GA status require further validation.

item.title: Extrusion-based bioprinting for functional tissue reconstruction: design strategies and applications
item.description: Extrusion-based bioprinting has become a widely used biofabrication strategy for tissue engineering because it enables controlled deposition of cell-laden bioinks, biomaterials, and bioactive factors into spatially organized constructs. In this review, we summarize the principles of extrusion-based bioprinting, including major printing configurations, emerging variants, bioink classifications, and key design criteria related to printability, rheology, crosslinking, and post-printing stability....

item.title: Application of multi-technique integration in the prenatal diagnosis of mosaicism derived from an ICSI blastocyst: a diagnostic approach and clinical implications
item.description: CONCLUSION: This case illustrates how the integration of CMA, G-banding, and targeted FISH enables accurate characterization of complex chromosomal rearrangements in prenatal diagnosis. While these findings underscore the importance of thorough evaluation in ART-conceived pregnancies, they do not establish a causal relationship between assisted reproduction and the observed chromosomal abnormality. The high-level mosaic duplication of 20p13p11.23 is associated with significant pathogenic risk....

item.title: Detection and Outcome Associations of Low-Grade Intraventricular Hemorrhage in Very Preterm Infants: Influence of Neuroimaging Modality and Grading System
item.description: CONCLUSION: Detection of intraventricular blood was associated with worse cognitive and motor outcomes. Differences between IVH grading systems and the choice of neuroimaging modality may influence risk stratification in infants with low-grade hemorrhage, particularly when small amounts of intraventricular blood are present.

item.title: Visual acuity changes in idebenone treatment‑naïve patients with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy: insights from the CRS-2 study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: CRS-2 provides insights into LHON natural history and suggests the disease course may be more dynamic than previously reported, with spontaneous VA changes occurring well into the chronic phase.

item.title: Immunological signatures of sepsis in abdominal solid organ transplant recipients: A multilayer and multicentric prospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSION: In patients with sepsis, abdominal SOT is associated with significant better survival than in non-SOT patients. Septic abdominal SOT patients display a distinct immune phenotype characterized by attenuated systemic inflammation, relative preservation of selected innate immune readouts, and alterations in immunometabolic markers.

item.title: Ventilator-associated pneumonia after traumatic brain injury: a timing-sensitive ecological framework of neuroimmune-pulmonary vulnerability
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This model proposes a timing-sensitive ecological framework in which established mechanisms may converge early and with particular clinical intensity after severe TBI, creating a vulnerable host-microbe state that may lower the threshold for clinically apparent infection. item.title: Internet Use and Knowledge of Clinical Trials Among US Adults: Cross-Sectional Survey Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Internet use is associated with greater CT knowledge. Thus, internet-based recruitment modalities may augment conventional engagement methods to identify US adults potentially interested in CT participation.
